formation.title: Restoration of the Song
formation.text:
The banners of the Song fly once more over Hangzhou. Where the dynasty once retreated south before the Jurchen onslaught, it now commands the wealthiest and most sophisticated realm in the world. The Yangtze valley teems with commerce, its cities dwarf any in Europe, and its innovations in paper money, gunpowder, and printing have no equal.

But the Song faces a choice that has defined it since its founding: what kind of power shall it be? The empire's strength has always lain not in its armies but in its merchants and scholars. Will the restored dynasty build upon its unrivaled maritime commerce, or turn inward to perfect the Neo-Confucian bureaucracy that makes governance itself an art?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Our ships shall carry Song wealth to every sea.

modifiers.name: Treasure of the Southern Seas
modifiers.text: With Hangzhou as its glittering capital, the restored Song commands the greatest maritime trade network in the known world, its harbors teeming with junks bearing silk, porcelain, and tea to every shore.

options.text: The examination hall is the foundation of empire.

modifiers.name: Mandate of the Brush
modifiers.text: The Song restoration places scholarship above all else. Through rigorous civil examinations and the wisdom of Neo-Confucian philosophy, the realm is governed by the learned rather than the powerful.

advances.name: Paddle-Wheel Tradition
advances.text: The Song navy pioneered paddle-wheel warships driven by treadmills, capable of remarkable speed and maneuverability on rivers and coastal waters.

event.title: Thunder on the Yangtze
event.text:
At the Battle of Caishi in 1161, Song paddle-wheel warships ambushed a far larger Jin transport fleet on the Yangtze. Thundercrash bombs launched from deck-mounted trebuchets shattered the enemy vessels while Song oarsmen drove their paddle-wheeled craft through the wreckage at speeds no conventional galley could match. The Jin force was annihilated, and the Yangtze line held.

This victory proves that innovation trumps numbers. Our naval engineers have mastered the paddle-wheel mechanism, producing vessels that can navigate upriver against the current, maneuver in narrow channels, and close rapidly on enemy ships. The question now is how to exploit this advantage.

options.text: Build an offensive fleet to carry the war north.

modifiers.name: River Dragons Unleashed
modifiers.text: The Song fleet strikes from the Yangtze, paddle-wheels churning and thundercrash bombs falling upon the enemy like hail.

options.text: Fortify the Yangtze: make our heartland invulnerable.

modifiers.name: The River Wall
modifiers.text: The Yangtze becomes an impassable barrier, fortified positions and patrol fleets denying any crossing to northern invaders.

advances.name: Jiaozi Currency System
advances.text: The world's first government-issued paper money, enabling a commercial economy of unprecedented scale.

event.title: The Paper Money Revolution
event.text:
In the markets of Hangzhou and Chengdu, merchants exchange slips of paper backed by the Song treasury, the world's first government-issued paper currency, the jiaozi. What began as private merchant drafts has become a revolution in finance. The printing bureaus at Huizhou and Hangzhou employ over a thousand workers each, producing the currency that lubricates a commercial economy of unprecedented scale.

Yet paper money is a double-edged sword. Too much in circulation breeds inflation and erodes trust. Too little starves commerce of the liquidity it needs to thrive. The court must decide: expand the money supply to fuel trade, or impose strict regulation to preserve fiscal stability?

options.text: Print more currency: commerce must flow freely.

modifiers.name: Currency Proliferation
modifiers.text: Paper money flows freely through Song markets, lubricating commerce and enriching merchants across the Yangtze.

options.text: Regulate the supply: stability above all.

modifiers.name: Fiscal Discipline
modifiers.text: Careful regulation of paper currency prevents inflation and strengthens the treasury's reserves.

advances.name: Song Iron Industry
advances.text: By 1078, Song China produced 125,000 tons of iron annually, a sixfold increase using coal-fired blast furnaces.

advances.name: Civilian Supremacy
advances.text: The Song principle of wen over wu, civilian authority over military, creating the most sophisticated bureaucratic state of its era.

advances.name: River Navy Levies
advances.text: The Song maintained a permanent river navy from 1132, the first standing navy in Chinese history, crewed by conscripted rivermen.

advances.name: Yangtze Defense Line
advances.text: The great river served as the Southern Song's primary defensive barrier, fortified with garrisons, signal beacons, and patrol fleets.

advances.name: Fire Lance Corps
advances.text: Song soldiers wielding fire lances, gunpowder-charged spears that projected flame and shrapnel, represented the world's first gunpowder infantry.

event.title: The Fire Lance Takes Shape
event.text:
Song alchemists and military engineers have perfected the fire lance, a bamboo or metal tube packed with gunpowder and projectiles, mounted on a spear shaft. In battle, the operator ignites the charge, sending a gout of flame and metal fragments into the enemy ranks before engaging with the spear. It is terrifying, devastating, and unlike anything the world has seen.

The Wujing Zongyao, our comprehensive military manual, records the formulas for gunpowder mixtures of varying strength. Fire lances are now being issued to infantry units stationed along the Yangtze defenses, giving Song soldiers a decisive advantage in close combat against superior northern cavalry.

options.text: The fire lance shall become our signature weapon.

advances.name: Fire Lance Levies
advances.text: Conscripted fire lance troops drawn from the general population, bringing early gunpowder weapons to the Song levy system.

advances.name: Movable Type Printing
advances.text: Bi Sheng's invention of ceramic movable type around 1040 revolutionized book production and made Song China the most literate society on earth.

event.title: Movable Type and the Printed Word
event.text:
The artisan Bi Sheng has devised a method of printing using individual ceramic characters arranged on an iron plate, coated in a mixture of pine resin and wax. When heated, the characters set firm; when cooled, they can be rearranged for the next page. Though woodblock printing remains dominant for large runs, Bi Sheng's movable type opens the possibility of printing any text without the expense of carving entire blocks.

Already the printing houses of Hangzhou produce more books in a single year than most kingdoms possess in their entire libraries. This technology, combined with Song paper-making expertise, is creating the most literate society the world has ever known.

options.text: Knowledge shall be the foundation of Song power.

advances.name: Neo-Confucian Synthesis
advances.text: Zhu Xi's commentaries on the Four Books unified Neo-Confucian philosophy and became the intellectual foundation of Chinese governance for seven centuries.

event.title: The Synthesis of Master Zhu
event.text:
The philosopher Zhu Xi has completed his monumental commentaries on the Four Books of the Confucian tradition, the Analects, the Mencius, the Great Learning, and the Doctrine of the Mean. His synthesis of earlier Neo-Confucian thought into a coherent philosophical system emphasizes li (principle) as the ordering force of the cosmos, and gewu (investigation of things) as the path to understanding.

Zhu Xi's work will reshape Chinese intellectual life for centuries. His commentaries can become the orthodox foundation of the examination system, producing officials steeped in moral philosophy, or his emphasis on investigation can be channeled toward practical governance and empirical inquiry.

options.text: Make the Four Books the sole foundation of learning.

modifiers.name: The Four Books Ascendant
modifiers.text: Zhu Xi's commentaries become the foundation of all learning, unifying the realm under a single moral philosophy.

options.text: Encourage the investigation of things in all domains.

modifiers.name: The Investigation of Things
modifiers.text: The Neo-Confucian emphasis on gewu, the investigation of things, drives practical scholarship and administrative efficiency.

advances.name: Commercial Revolution
advances.text: The Song economic transformation, from agricultural tribute state to commercial powerhouse, driven by urbanization, paper money, and maritime trade.

advances.name: Tea Trade Networks
advances.text: Tea became the Song dynasty's most important commercial commodity, with government-licensed tea houses serving as hubs for trade and cultural exchange.

advances.name: Tower Ship Construction
advances.text: Multi-decked armored warships carrying hundreds of soldiers and deck-mounted trebuchets, dominating both river and coastal warfare.

advances.name: Thundercrash Weapons
advances.text: Iron-cased gunpowder bombs launched from trebuchets, named for the terrifying sound they produced, an early form of explosive artillery.

advances.name: Compass Navigation
advances.text: Song mariners pioneered the use of the magnetic compass for maritime navigation, enabling reliable ocean voyages to Southeast Asia and beyond.

advances.name: Porcelain Export Mastery
advances.text: Song celadon and white porcelain became the most sought-after luxury goods across Asia and the Indian Ocean world.

advances.name: Legal Codification
advances.text: Systematic revision and compilation of Song legal codes, creating one of the most comprehensive legal systems of the medieval world.

advances.name: Maritime Silk Route
advances.text: With overland routes cut off by hostile steppe powers, Song merchants established maritime trade routes carrying silk, porcelain, and tea across the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Ironclad Paddle-Wheels
advances.text: By 1203, Song engineers were armoring paddle-wheel warships with iron plates, creating the world's first ironclad vessels.

advances.name: Hangzhou Trade Junk Fleet
advances.text: Fast, seaworthy junks based in Hangzhou, combining merchant cargo capacity with defensive armament for long-range ocean trade.

advances.name: Iron-Cased Bombs
advances.text: The transition from soft-shelled to iron-cased gunpowder bombs dramatically increased their lethality and blast radius.

advances.name: Waterway Mastery
advances.text: The Song mastery of canals, locks, and river transport created an internal trade network unmatched anywhere in the world.

advances.name: Examination Reform
advances.text: Expansion and refinement of the civil service examination system, widening access to government service based purely on merit.

advances.name: Rice Paddy Intensification
advances.text: Introduction of early-ripening Champa rice varieties and double-cropping techniques dramatically increased food production in the Yangtze valley.

advances.name: Song Naval Supremacy
advances.text: The culmination of centuries of naval innovation (paddle-wheels, gunpowder armaments, iron cladding) establishing unchallenged dominance on water.

advances.name: Advanced Monetary Policy
advances.text: Sophisticated management of paper currency supply, interest rates, and government reserves, pioneering modern fiscal practices.

advances.name: Industrial Ironworks
advances.text:
Expansion of coal-fired blast furnaces to industrial scale, producing steel for weapons, tools, and infrastructure across the realm.

Available in: Song Iron Foundry

advances.name: Literary Compilations
advances.text: The Song tradition of encyclopedic compilations, preserving and systematizing knowledge across every domain from astronomy to agriculture.

advances.name: Coastal Defense Modernization
advances.text: Fortification of the southern coastline with batteries, watchtowers, and patrol fleets to protect Song maritime commerce.

advances.name: Industrial Modernization
advances.text: Application of Song engineering traditions to modern industrial production, mechanizing workshops and expanding output.

advances.name: Maritime Modernization
advances.text: Modernization of the Song merchant and naval fleet, incorporating advances in shipbuilding and navigation technology.

advances.name: Constitutional Reform
advances.text: Formalization of the Song meritocratic tradition into constitutional principles of governance and rule of law.

advances.name: Modern Education System
advances.text: Transformation of the Neo-Confucian academy system into a modern educational network, maintaining the Song tradition of universal literacy.

advances.name: Yangtze Delta Industry
advances.text: The Yangtze delta, already the most productive region on earth, becomes the engine of a modern industrial economy.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Song
destiny.text: The Song dynasty has risen again. Now the restored empire must chart its future: will it look outward across the seas, or inward to perfect the art of governance?

event.title: The Song Endures
event.text: Against all odds, the Song dynasty has survived its crises and emerged stronger than before. The scholars of the Academy speak of a renewed Mandate: a dynasty that has proven itself through perseverance and good governance. Whether the future lies upon the waves or within the examination halls, the Song shall write the next chapter of its long history.

options.text: The Song shall endure for ten thousand years.

destiny.name: The Fujian Entrepots
destiny.text: Quanzhou and Zhangzhou are the greatest ports in the world. Secure them, fill the treasury, and the oceans shall open before us.

conditions.text: Own Jìnjiāng, or a subject owns it
Own Lóngxī, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Ports of Fujian
event.text:
The great harbor of Quanzhou (known to Arab merchants as Zayton) and the bustling entrepot of Zhangzhou are now firmly under Song control. Together with the workshops of Hangzhou, they form a commercial triangle of unmatched wealth. Foreign merchants from Arabia, India, and the Spice Islands crowd the wharves, trading pepper and incense for Song silk and porcelain.

The Superintendent of Maritime Trade reports customs revenues beyond anything the treasury has seen. The oceans themselves seem to beckon.

options.text: Let the Song banner fly above every mast.

destiny.name: Lords of the Nanyang
destiny.text: The spice islands and the Strait of Malacca are the chokepoints of maritime Asia. Song treasure fleets must command these waters.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Palembang, or a subject owns it

event.title: Mastery of the Nanyang
event.text:
Song influence now stretches across the South China Sea to the Strait of Malacca. Our merchants dominate the trade in spices, camphor, and tropical hardwoods that flows through these waters. The great entrepots of Palembang and Malacca, once independent kingdoms, now operate under Song commercial supervision.

This achievement has no precedent in Chinese history. The dynasty that was mocked for retreating south has built something no northern empire ever possessed: a maritime sphere of influence spanning thousands of li.

options.text: Monopolize the spice trade at its source.

modifiers.name: Spice Trade Monopoly
modifiers.text: Song control of the Nanyang trade routes has created a near-monopoly on the flow of spices to East Asian markets.

options.text: Bind these kingdoms to the Song as tributaries.

modifiers.name: Nanyang Tributary Network
modifiers.text: The maritime kingdoms of Southeast Asia acknowledge Song suzerainty, sending tribute missions and receiving trade privileges in return.

destiny.name: Masters of Every Sea
destiny.text: From the Malabar Coast to the Persian Gulf, Song merchants shall trade in every port. No sea shall be closed to our fleets.

conditions.text: Own Kozhikode, or a subject owns it
Own Hormuz, or a subject owns it
Own Temasek, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Song Oceans
event.text:
Song treasure fleets now anchor in the harbors of India and the Persian Gulf. The compass-guided junks of Hangzhou carry porcelain and silk to markets that once seemed impossibly distant. At Calicut, Song merchants negotiate alongside Arab traders. At Hormuz, the gateway to the Mediterranean trade, Song goods command premium prices.

This is a commercial empire without parallel: built not on conquest alone, but on the superiority of Song navigation, shipbuilding, and the sheer volume of luxury goods our workshops produce.

options.text: Continue Zheng He's vision of peaceful exploration.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Treasure Fleets
modifiers.text: Song treasure fleets range across the Indian Ocean, projecting maritime power and commercial influence to every shore.

options.text: Assert the Song Mandate over these waters.

modifiers.name: Maritime Mandate
modifiers.text: The Song claim sovereignty over the seas themselves, enforcing trading standards and collecting tolls at every chokepoint.

destiny.name: Order of the Southern Realm
destiny.text: Before the Song can look north, it must perfect governance in the south. Hold Hangzhou, print the realm's paper money there again in a Paper Currency Bureau, raise its development to 48, and forge a bureaucracy without equal.

conditions.text: Hangzhou is owned and has a Paper Currency Bureau
Hangzhou is owned and has development of at least 48

event.title: A Well-Ordered Realm
event.text:
The southern provinces have been transformed. Where once there was frontier wilderness and restive minorities, there are now thriving cities connected by canals, governed by examination-selected magistrates, and linked to the capital through an efficient postal system. The paper money of the Hangzhou bureau finances development across the realm.

The scholars say that this is what the ancient sages envisioned: governance through moral example and bureaucratic competence, not through force. The south is ready to serve as the foundation for greater things.

options.text: The south is well-ordered. What comes next?

destiny.name: Reclaiming the Central Plains
destiny.text: Kaifeng and Luoyang, the old Song capitals, must be returned to the dynasty. The northern frontier must be secured by force of arms.

conditions.text: Own Kāifēng, or a subject owns it
Own Luòyáng, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Return to the North
event.text:
Song banners fly once more over Kaifeng and Luoyang, the ancient capitals where the dynasty was born. The restoration of the northern heartland has been the dream of every Song patriot since the Jurchen invasion drove the court south. The old Imperial Way in Kaifeng is being rebuilt, its marketplaces and pleasure quarters restored to their former glory.

But the north has changed in the centuries of foreign rule. Its people have adopted different customs, its fields lie partially fallow, and its cities have shrunk. The question is whether to reconquer aggressively or integrate patiently.

options.text: Press the reconquest: the north must be freed.

modifiers.name: Reconquest Fervor
modifiers.text: The liberation of the old capitals has ignited patriotic fervor across the realm. Song armies march north with the zeal of a righteous cause, and the court's purse is emptied to keep them marching.

options.text: Integrate the north gradually into Song order.

modifiers.name: Northern Integration
modifiers.text: Patient administration and cultural outreach gradually restore Song identity in the long-alienated northern provinces. Every statute must now be made to fit the north as well as the south.

destiny.name: The Mandate Perfected
destiny.text: With the old capitals restored and Dadu itself under Song control, the dynasty must rebuild Kaifeng to a development of 73, twice what it was, and reach a prestige that proves the Mandate of Heaven is truly theirs.

conditions.text: Own Dàdū, or a subject owns it
Kaifeng is owned and has development of at least 73

event.title: The Perfect Dynasty
event.text:
From Hangzhou in the south to Dadu in the north, the Song dynasty now governs the most developed, most literate, and most prosperous realm the world has ever known. The civil examination system selects the best minds regardless of birth. The imperial library preserves the accumulated wisdom of three millennia. The land produces more rice, iron, silk, and porcelain than any other civilization.

Scholars speak of a new golden age: one that surpasses even the legendary era of the Three Sovereigns. The Song has not merely restored the Mandate of Heaven; it has perfected it.

options.text: Build an eternal bureaucracy to outlast any dynasty.

modifiers.name: The Eternal Bureaucracy
modifiers.text: A perfected examination system and comprehensive legal code create a bureaucracy that can govern effectively regardless of who sits upon the throne.

options.text: Patronize a renaissance of arts and learning.

modifiers.name: Song Renaissance
modifiers.text: The Song court becomes the patron of a new golden age of arts, letters, and natural philosophy, attracting scholars from across the known world.

units.name: Paddle-Wheel Warship
units.text: A treadmill-driven vessel of remarkable speed, armed with deck-mounted trebuchets for hurling gunpowder bombs. Song paddle-wheelers could outmaneuver any contemporary galley.

units.name: Paddle-Wheel Warship
units.text: A conscripted paddle-wheel vessel from the Song river fleet.

units.name: Fire Lance Infantry
units.text: Elite soldiers wielding fire lances, gunpowder-packed tubes mounted on spear shafts that project flame and shrapnel before the wielder closes to melee. A terrifying weapon unique to Song warfare.

units.name: Fire Lance Militia
units.text: Conscripted infantry equipped with fire lances, bringing gunpowder weapons to the Song levy system.

units.name: Tower Ship
units.text: A multi-decked armored warship carrying hundreds of soldiers and deck-mounted trebuchets. Tower ships dominated river and coastal combat through sheer size and firepower.

units.name: Thundercrash Bombard
units.text: Early gunpowder artillery hurling iron-cased explosive bombs with devastating effect. Named for the terrifying crash of their detonation.

units.name: Ironclad Galley
units.text: A paddle-wheel warship armored with riveted iron plates, combining the speed of a galley with unprecedented protection against enemy fire.

units.name: Hangzhou Trade Junk
units.text: A fast, seaworthy merchant vessel from Hangzhou, armed for self-defense on the maritime silk route. These junks carried Song goods as far as East Africa.

buildings.name: Song Iron Foundry
buildings.text: A coal-fired blast furnace complex producing iron and steel at industrial scale. By 1078, Song foundries produced more iron than England would manage seven centuries later.

where.text: The location's raw material is Iron

buildings.name: Paper Currency Bureau
buildings.text: A government printing office producing jiaozi paper currency, employing over a thousand workers to mint the world's first fiat money.

buildings.name: Song Naval Shipyard
buildings.text: A specialized facility for constructing paddle-wheel warships, with treadmill-testing yards and iron-fitting workshops.

buildings.name: Song Printing House
buildings.text: A publishing facility producing books using both woodblock and movable type techniques, supplying the most literate society on earth.

buildings.name: Gunpowder Arsenal
buildings.text: A weapons research and manufacturing center producing fire lances, thundercrash bombs, and gunpowder mixtures according to the Wujing Zongyao formulas.

buildings.name: Song Tea House
buildings.text: A licensed commercial and cultural establishment where merchants negotiate deals over elaborate tea ceremonies, serving as a hub for both trade and literati culture.

buildings.name: Yangtze River Fort
buildings.text: A fortified garrison commanding a strategic point on the Yangtze, part of the Southern Song's river defense network that held the line against northern invasion for over a century.

buildings.name: Academy of Learning
buildings.text: A Neo-Confucian study center dedicated to the teachings of Zhu Xi, where scholar-officials pursue the investigation of things and the cultivation of moral character.

buildings.name: Silkworm House
buildings.text: The silkworm room of a Jiangnan farm household, among the mulberry groves of Huzhou and Jiaxing. The women of the house strip the leaves, feed the worms through their sleeps and reel the cocoons in hot water, and the household pays its summer tax in silk. It raises the silk the land itself gives.

where.text: The location's raw material is Silk

buildings.name: Song Porcelain Kiln
buildings.text: A celadon firing facility producing the distinctive jade-green porcelain that became the most sought-after luxury commodity across Asia and the Indian Ocean world.

buildings.name: Treasure Fleet Harbor
buildings.text: A massive purpose-built harbor facility capable of constructing, outfitting, and supplying the enormous treasure fleet junks that project Song power across every ocean.

buildings.name: Imperial Library
buildings.text: The greatest repository of knowledge in the world, housing millions of volumes covering every branch of learning. The Imperial Library preserves and systematizes the accumulated wisdom of Chinese civilization.

list.name: The Three Departments
list.text: Sansheng (the Zhongshu (drafting), Menxia (review), and Shangshu (execution) departments) formed the apex of Tang and Song imperial governance. Every imperial edict passed through the Zhongshu Sheng's chancellors for drafting, the Menxia Sheng's right of formal remonstrance, and only then the Shangshu Sheng for execution by the Six Boards beneath it. The Song refined the system into its most articulate form before the Yongle Emperor abolished the chancellorship in 1380; functioning well, the Three Departments produced consensus law and stable governance, but rival chancellors could deadlock decrees for years.

list.name: The Song Examination System
list.text: Founded under the Sui in 605, the keju reached unprecedented scale and prestige under the Song. By the late Northern Song roughly 50,000 candidates sat the prefectural exams each cycle, with successful jinshi entering a guaranteed civil career. Wang Anshi's 1071 curriculum reform replaced poetic composition with practical policy-essay (cewen) on the meanings of the classics, breaking the aristocracy's literary monopoly and producing a deeply literate scholar-official elite. The system also bred bitter factional cliques and, in periods of decay, rampant cheating and the sale of degrees.

list.name: Remonstrance Bureau
list.text: The Song gave criticism an office of its own. The Remonstrance Bureau was founded around 1017 and fully staffed from 1032 under Emperor Renzong. Censors impeached officials. Remonstrators went further: they read what passed between the emperor and his ministers and argued against the policy itself. In 1050 Bao Zheng, serving there, fought the promotion of the uncle of the emperor's favourite consort until the emperor took half of it back. A bureau captured by a faction became that faction's weapon, as in the purges that undid Wang Anshi's reforms.

list.name: Hanlin Academy
list.text: Founded under Tang Xuanzong and elevated by Song Taizu in 960, the Hanlin Yuan was the academy of the brush, the empire's most prestigious literary institute. Hanlin academicians drafted imperial edicts of the highest grade, compiled the dynastic histories, and tutored the heir apparent. The Song Hanlin produced the era's defining literati: Ouyang Xiu, Sima Guang, Su Shi, and Wang Anshi himself all served within its walls. A vigorous academy lent the throne unmatched cultural prestige; a coddled one fractured into Yuanyou and Shaosheng factions whose endorsements grew hollow.

list.name: Wang Anshi's New Policies
list.text: The Xinfa reform program of Chancellor Wang Anshi (1069-1076) attempted the most ambitious restructuring of Song governance. Qing miao extended state spring loans to peasants at lower rates than village moneylenders; junshu pingtiao stockpiled grain in state warehouses to dampen famine speculation; the baojia organized rural households into mutual-responsibility militias; and the shi yi fa market-exchange offices brought commercial regulation under the state. The program split the elite into Reformist and Conservative factions whose feud raged for two generations.

list.name: Salt and Tea Monopoly
list.text: The Yan-Cha Si commissions managed the Song state's monopolies on salt, tea, and (in some periods) alum, liquor, and incense. Salt revenue alone supplied roughly half of Northern Song state income at peak. Licensed merchants purchased transport tickets (yan-yin) from regional commissions, while the cha-fa offices regulated the Yangzi tea trade in exchange for frontier horse imports from the Tibetans and Tanguts. The system enriched the treasury and the licensed merchants but invited rampant smuggling, salt-cartel abuses, and peasant resentment of inflated prices.

list.name: Jiao Shu Printing Office
list.text: The Song state printing apparatus made Song China the most literate, monetarily sophisticated society of its age. The Imperial Press at Kaifeng and Hangzhou produced authoritative editions of the Confucian classics, the Twenty-Four Histories, the Buddhist Tripitaka, and after 1040 the movable-type experiments of Bi Sheng. The Jiaozi bureau, established in Chengdu in 1023, issued the world's first government-printed paper currency against copper reserves. Mismanaged, the bureau's over-issue of notes triggered the inflationary collapses that plagued the late Northern and Southern Song treasuries.
